modules.title: Lesson 1.1: Self & Identity (Ich heiße / Ich bin)
modules.canDo: Greet someone and introduce yourself using Ich heiße or Ich bin.
modules.concept: In German statements, the conjugated verb always sits in second position (V2): 'Ich heiße Anna' or 'Ich bin Lukas'.

model.en: Hello! What is your name? — Hello! My name is Anna.

options.text: In second position right after the subject
At the very end of the sentence

modules.title: Lesson 1.2: Professions & Roles (Ich bin / Das ist)
modules.canDo: State your profession or role without an article, and identify objects with ein / eine.
modules.concept: When stating professions in German, drop the article: 'Ich bin Lehrer' (I am a teacher). Use 'ein' (masculine/neuter) or 'eine' (feminine) when pointing out things with 'Das ist'.

model.en: Are you a student? — Yes, I am a student. She is a teacher.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Ja, ich bin Student. Sie ist Lehrerin.
turns.en: Yes, I am a student. She is a teacher.

check.question: How do you naturally say 'I am a teacher' in German?

options.text: Ich bin Lehrer. / Ich bin Lehrerin.

modules.title: Lesson 1.3: Origins & Countries (kommen aus)
modules.canDo: Ask and state which city or country someone comes from using kommen aus.
modules.concept: Use 'kommen aus' (to come from) followed by a city or country: 'Ich komme aus Berlin', 'Er kommt aus Österreich'.

modules.title: Lesson 2.1: Everyday Present Actions
modules.canDo: Describe what you and others do or are doing right now using regular present verbs.
modules.concept: German uses a single present tense for both 'I work' and 'I am working'. Regular verb endings: ich -e, du -st, er/sie -t, wir -en.

model.context: Checking in with a study partner:
model.en: What are you doing today? — I am studying German.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.en: I am studying German and working.

check.question: How do you express 'I am studying German' in German?

drills.explanation: Regular German present statements place the conjugated verb second.

modules.title: Lesson 2.2: Feelings & Wellbeing (Wie geht es dir?)
modules.canDo: Ask how someone is doing and describe how you feel.
modules.concept: Ask 'Wie geht es dir?' (How is it going for you?) and reply 'Mir geht es gut'. For specific feelings like tired or happy, use 'Ich bin müde' / 'Ich bin glücklich'.

vocab.meaning: I am doing (lit. to me it goes)

turns.en: I am doing well, thanks! I am happy.

modules.title: Lesson 2.3: Past Actions (Perfekt with haben)
modules.canDo: Talk about what you did yesterday using the Perfekt tense (haben + ge-...-t).
modules.concept: Spoken German forms the past tense with a 'sentence bracket': 'haben' stays in second position, while the past participle ('gelernt', 'gearbeitet') goes to the very end.

model.en: What did you do yesterday? — Yesterday I studied German.

check.question: Where does the past participle ('gelernt') go in a German Perfekt sentence?

options.text: At the very end of the sentence

drills.explanation: Perfekt brackets the sentence with 'haben' in V2 and the participle at the end.

modules.title: Lesson 3.1: Static Locations (im / in der / zu Hause)
modules.canDo: Ask and state where people are right now using im, in der, and zu Hause.
modules.concept: For static location ('where?'), 'in' takes the dative: 'in dem' contracts to 'im' (masculine/neuter, e.g. 'im Büro'), and feminine nouns use 'in der' (e.g. 'in der Schule'). 'At home' is 'zu Hause'.

model.en: Where are you? — I am at the office.

check.question: Why does 'in dem Büro' shorten to 'im Büro'?

options.text: 'in + dem' contracts naturally to 'im' in German

drills.explanation: Neuter 'das Büro' becomes 'im Büro' (in + dem) for static location.

Match the sentence to its pattern
drills.explanation: Static places use 'sein' + dative preposition ('im / in der').

modules.title: Lesson 3.2: Relative Position (auf / unter / vor)
modules.canDo: Specify whether an object is on, under, next to, or in front of a landmark.
modules.concept: Spatial prepositions 'auf' (on), 'unter' (under), 'neben' (next to), and 'vor' (in front of) take the dative for static positions: 'auf dem Tisch' (on the table).

model.context: Finding a book on a desk:
model.en: Where is the book? — The book is on the table.
model.target: Das Buch ist auf dem Tisch.
model.literal: [The book = Das Buch] + [is = ist] + [on = auf] + [the table = dem Tisch]

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Das Buch ist auf dem Tisch.
turns.en: The book is on the table.

modules.title: Lesson 3.3: Movement & Destinations (nach / in / zu)
modules.canDo: Say where you are going using nach (cities/home), in (buildings), and zu (people/places).
modules.concept: Use 'nach' for cities, most countries, and 'nach Hause' (homeward). Use 'ins' (in + das) or 'in die' when entering a building or space.

model.context: Heading out at the end of the day:
model.en: Where are you going? — I am going home now.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Ich gehe nach Hause. Morgen fahre ich nach Berlin.
turns.en: I am going home. Tomorrow I travel to Berlin.

modules.title: Lesson 4.1: Completed States (schon fertig / bereit)
modules.canDo: Announce that tasks, meals, or plans are already finished or ready using schon + fertig / bereit.
modules.concept: Combine 'ist / sind' with 'schon' (already) and a state adjective like 'fertig' (finished/ready) or 'bereit' (prepared).

model.en: Is the work finished? — Yes, the work is already finished!
model.literal: [The work = Die Arbeit] + [is = ist] + [already = schon] + [finished = fertig]

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Ja, die Arbeit ist schon fertig!
turns.en: Yes, the work is already finished!

modules.title: Lesson 4.2: Obligations & Plans (müssen / wollen)
modules.canDo: Express what you must, should, or want to do using German modal verb brackets.
modules.concept: Modal verbs ('muss' must, 'will' want, 'soll' should) stand in second position and send the main action verb in its infinitive form ('gehen', 'lernen') to the very end.

model.context: Deciding next steps with your group:
model.en: We have to go now. — Yes, I must work tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.en: Yes, I have to work tomorrow.

check.question: In 'Wir müssen jetzt gehen', why is 'gehen' at the end?

options.text: Modal verbs push the main infinitive verb to the end of the clause

prompts.situation: Tell the group that you all have to go now:

drills.instruction: Choose the infinitive form at the end
drills.explanation: After a modal verb, the final verb stays in the infinitive ('arbeiten').

drills.instruction: Match the sentence to its pattern
drills.explanation: Modal verb in V2 + infinitive at the end is the German modal bracket.

modules.title: Lesson 4.3: Explaining Why (weil)
modules.canDo: Give clear reasons by joining two clauses with weil (because) and verb-final word order.
modules.concept: 'weil' ('because') kicks the conjugated verb of the second clause to the very end: 'Ich bin glücklich, weil die Arbeit fertig ist.'

model.context: Explaining why you are smiling at the end of the day:
model.en: I am happy because the work is finished.
model.target: Ich bin glücklich, weil die Arbeit fertig ist.
model.literal: [I am happy] + [because = weil] + [the work finished is]

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Ich bin glücklich, weil die Arbeit fertig ist.
turns.en: I am happy because the work is finished.

check.question: Where does the conjugated verb ('ist' / 'bin') go inside a 'weil' clause?

options.text: At the very end of the 'weil' clause
